## What the chronicles say [Record]

In spring 1384 Jogaila had offered Volhynia with Lutsk, which [Vytautas](../characters/vytautas.qmd) refused, demanding his Trakai patrimony; in July 1384 the two reconciled and Vytautas abandoned the Order, burning its castles (see [the burnings](ev_burnings_1384.qmd)). The terms: Grodno, Brest and Podlasie for Vytautas; Trakai stayed with Skirgaila, who had held it since 1382 (Jogaila had promised it to Vytautas in spring 1384 once Skirgaila was settled in Polotsk). Marquard von Salzbach was captured in July 1384. The meeting itself has no documented place or witnesses. Sources: Posilge, Wigand, the Lithuanian chronicles; Kiaupa and Ivinskis in modern writing.

## What really happened [Saga]

A secret parley in a roofless burnt church at the edge of the Šventaragis grove, with a red dot of fire in the valley below. Jogaila arrives with four guards, no banners or trumpets; Vytautas comes alone in the Order's battered armour with the cross torn off. Between them lies Kęstutis's blood. Jogaila says that the Order stood at Trakai: it was the cross or the fire. No forgiveness, only a truce of necessity. Henė knocks two stones together in the dark; Vytautas shows the silver wolf amulet and does not kill. It is the first time since Krėva they have looked each other in the eye.

## Consequences

Caused by [the burnings of 1384](ev_burnings_1384.qmd). It leads to [Birutė's Amber Sacrifice](ev_birute_sacrifice.qmd); the autumn settlement confirms [Skirgaila's hold on Trakai](ev_trakai_to_skirgaila.qmd).

## Dramatisation

Book I ch. 26 "Susitikimas Peleninėje" (Vytautas and Jogaila; a July night in 1384, Vilnius; the text keeps an older 'late summer 1383' cue).
